newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Cookson H1 profit flat, sees H2 up.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Cookson H1 profit flat, sees H2 up.

text.p: British conglomerate Cookson Group Plc on Thursday said it expected profit growth to resume in the second half of 1997 after flat results in the first six months.

Pre-tax profit was 85.4 million pounds ($143.1 million) in the first half compared with 85.3 million a year ago. The results were affected by the strong pound, and at constant exchange rates Cookson said profit was nine percent ahead.
The result was slightly better than expected and Cookson shares rose to 229 before easing to 219, a gain of 4-1/2 pence.
Profit growth will resume in the second half because results in the electronics division will improve as the industry de-stocking process is over.
"We enter the second half with a very strong order book, we have new products coming to the market place and we see good prospects going forward," chief executive Richard Oster said.
He said full-year profits would be in line with market expectations, which centre around pre-tax profit of 180 million pounds.
Oster will become chairman on October 1, taking over from Robert Malpas who will retire. Oster, meanwhile, will be replaced by Stephen Howard, who currently is joint group managing director.
Malpas said the transition would be "seamless" and added there would not be any change in Cookson's strategy.
"We are very pleased that we are promoting from within the company and that immediately implies that there will be a clear continuity," Malpas said.
Cookson said the turnaround in the electronics division is now underway, while it also saw sound prospects for its engineered products, advanced refractories and plastics divisions.
At Cookson Matthey Ceramics (CMC), the joint venture with Johnson Matthey Plc, profits from the zircon activities are seen unchanged.
But the other businesses at CMC, which represent about three quarters of the division, continue to improve, Cookson said.
At constant exchange rates, operating profits in the electronics division rose four percent in the first half with the rate of organic growth improving each month.
Profits in the advanced refractories division increased by 34 percent. Results were boosted by the contribution from Monofrax from the U.S., which was bought at the end of 1996.
CMC saw operating profits fall 50 percent due to the zircon business which suffered from a margins squeeze. But results in other activities improved markedly, Cookson said.
In engineered products, the precious metals sector performed well, while the contacts and stampings sector had an excellent first half.

Operating profit, excluding the results from the Cookson Pigments Business which was sold late last year, rose 13 percent in the plastics division in the first half of 1997. ($ = 0.596 British Pounds)
